chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the believer intends a good deed but does not perform it, so one good deed is recorded for him; and if he performs it, ten good deeds are recorded for him. And indeed, the believer intends an evil deed that he would perform, but he does not perform it, so it is not recorded against him.
ai.seo_question: How are good and evil deeds recorded in Shia Islam based on intention and action?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of 'al-Hasanah bi-l-Qasdi' (the good deed by intention), emphasizing that mere sincere intent for a good deed earns a reward even before execution, while abstaining from a sin due to restraint is counted as a good deed. This mechanism underscores the divine mercy in valuing internal spiritual states and the struggle against the self (jihad al-nafs), distinguishing it from the mere absence of action.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from usman Bin isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin intends the good deed and does not do it, so one good deed is Written for him; and if he were to do it, ten good deeds would be Written for him; but if the Momin intends the evil deed that he would be doing it, but he does not do it, so it would not be Written against him’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’a ibn Mehran from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

A believer may intend to perform a good deed but does not do it, still (the reward for) one good deed will be written for him and if he actually completes it, (the reward for) ten good deeds will be written in his favor. A believer may intend to commit an evil deed but if he does not do it, nothing will be written against him.”
